lens_summary: m9-75 closes the medium finding m9-70 and m9-73 both deferred: ChronosServer::open_default_store opened the configured store and, on any failure, logged a warning and continued with an empty in-memory store, so a server pointed at a store that exists but cannot be opened (locked by a second process, corrupt, permission denied) started successfully, answered session_save with success, answered session_list with nothing and reported healthy - silent data loss behind a green health check. The policy is now explicit and testable as three pure functions: default_store_path(db_path, home) resolves $CHRONOS_DB_PATH or $HOME/.local/share/chronos/sessions.redb with empty values falling through, allow_in_memory_fallback(raw) accepts only 1/true/yes trimmed and case-insensitive, and open_store_at(path, allow_in_memory_fallback) returns Result<SessionStore, StoreOpenError> and degrades only when the caller opted in. StoreOpenError is Debug + Display + Error, names the path and the cause and the opt-in, and boxes its cause so clippy::result_large_err stays quiet. ChronosServer::try_new() is the new entrypoint, new() panics with the same message, and crates/chronos-mcp/src/bin/chronos-mcp.rs uses try_new() and exits 2 with 'chronos-mcp: fatal: <message>' on stderr before the transport starts. The interesting verification problem is observability: the policy is invisible through the MCP tool surface, because a degraded server and a healthy server answer the same tools with different data, and it is visible in the process exit status - so chronos-sandbox/tests/store_open_failure.rs spawns the real binary with CHRONOS_DB_PATH pointing at a directory (exists, so the missing-parent allowance cannot excuse it, and can never be a redb database) and asserts exit 2 plus a stderr line naming the path and the cause, then starts the same fixture with CHRONOS_ALLOW_IN_MEMORY_FALLBACK=1 and asserts the server does serve, so the opt-in is demonstrably the difference and the fixture is demonstrably unopenable. Falsification was done twice: reverting open_store_at's Err branch to the unconditional in-memory fallback fails test_open_store_at_fails_closed_instead_of_degrading_silently at server.rs:6237, and rebuilding the binary with that revert fails test_server_refuses_to_start_when_the_configured_store_cannot_be_opened with ExitStatus(unix_wait_status(256)) instead of Some(2); both restored byte-identically (cmp against the scratch backup) before the green runs. A third observation kept the cycle honest: the first acceptance run was green for the wrong reason because the sandbox resolve_mcp_path() ladder preferred a stale target/debug/chronos-mcp built before this cycle, so the assertion text showed the pre-m9-75 'Using in-memory store.' warning; the binary was rebuilt, the run repeated, and AGENTS.md now records the hazard.

findings.summary: Closed: the server no longer replaces a store it cannot open with an empty in-memory one. It fails closed with a named error, exits 2 before serving, and only degrades when CHRONOS_ALLOW_IN_MEMORY_FALLBACK is exactly 1/true/yes. Observable in the exit status of the real binary, which is what the new sandbox suite asserts.

subject.gap: crates/chronos-mcp/src/server.rs::open_default_store (both the production and the cfg(test) variants) called SessionStore::try_open(path) and, on Err, logged 'Could not open session store at {path}: {cause}. Using in-memory store.' at warn level and returned SessionStore::in_memory(). Nothing else in the process noticed: session_save wrote into a store that would be discarded, session_list answered with an empty list, and no tool reported the degraded mode, so a client could not distinguish 'your store is empty' from 'your store was ignored'. Triggering conditions are a real store that is locked by another process (two chronos-mcp instances against one $CHRONOS_DB_PATH), corrupt, or unreadable (permissions), i.e. exactly the cases where the persisted data matters. Detection existed only by accident: m9-73's client_store_isolation fails if it ever runs against a fallback store, but that is a sandbox test, not production behaviour.
subject.fix: crates/chronos-mcp/src/server.rs: pub struct StoreOpenError { path: PathBuf, cause: Box<chronos_store::StoreError> } with path(), cause(), Display (names the path, the cause and CHRONOS_ALLOW_IN_MEMORY_FALLBACK) and Error::source() returning the store error; fn default_store_path(db_path, home) resolving $CHRONOS_DB_PATH then $HOME/.local/share/chronos/sessions.redb with empty values falling through; fn allow_in_memory_fallback(raw) accepting only Some(1|true|yes) after trim + to_ascii_lowercase; fn open_store_at(path, allow_in_memory_fallback) returning Result<SessionStore, StoreOpenError> where the Err branch is fail-closed and the allow branch logs the failure at error level before degrading; pub fn try_new() -> Result<Self, StoreOpenError> as the new constructor and new() panicking with the error message; try_open_default_store() returning Result in both cfg(test) and production variants. crates/chronos-mcp/src/bin/chronos-mcp.rs: try_new() and, on Err, tracing::error! plus eprintln!('chronos-mcp: fatal: {e}') plus std::process::exit(2) before the transport starts. chronos-sandbox/src/client/tools.rs: resolve_mcp_path() made public. Tests: four in server.rs (path resolution precedence including empty values, strictness of the opt-in across seven inputs, parent-directory creation for a missing path, and the fail-closed/opt-in/differential-reopen triple for an unopenable path) and a new binary-level suite chronos-sandbox/tests/store_open_failure.rs (138 lines, 2 tests). Docs: docs/manual-ai/en/08-session-management.md and docs/manual-ai/es/08-gestion-sesiones.md gain a 'When the store cannot be opened' section, and AGENTS.md records that the sandbox binary lookup uses the last built binary.

deferred.note: New, deliberately deferred. With CHRONOS_ALLOW_IN_MEMORY_FALLBACK=1 the server runs exactly as before: the failure is logged at error level to stderr, but no MCP response mentions it, so a client that opts into the degraded mode still cannot tell from a session_save/session_list payload that nothing is being persisted. The finding this cycle closed was about the *silent* part of the fallback, and refusing to start removes the silence for the default configuration; surfacing the mode in tool responses (a field on the session tools' envelope, or a capabilities flag) is an API-shape decision with callers to update, and the opt-in path is not the one users get by accident. Not attempted here.
deferred.severity_rationale: Requires an explicit opt-in to reach, and the operator who sets it has already accepted that nothing is persisted; no silent loss without that opt-in.
